  <Company Condition="'$(Company)' == ''">Contoso</Company>
  ...
</PropertyGroup>
```

---

### 3. `LibA/LibA.csproj` (line 13) — Unquoted `Condition` value

```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="$(Configuration) == Debug">
```

**Problem:** The condition is missing quotes around `$(Configuration)` **and** `Debug`. If `$(Configuration)` is empty (e.g., during NuGet restore or IDE evaluation without explicit configuration), the expression becomes ` == Debug` which is an MSBuild evaluation error. Even when it works, this is fragile.

**Fix:**
```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(Configuration)' == 'Debug'">
```

---

### 4. `LibA/LibA.csproj` (line 14) — `DefineConstants` overwrites SDK defaults

```xml
<DefineConstants>ENABLE_LOGGING</DefineConstants>
```

**Problem:** This replaces the SDK-provided constants (`DEBUG`, `TRACE`) instead of appending. Code guarded by `#if DEBUG` or `#if TRACE` will silently stop working in Debug builds.

**Fix:**
```xml
<DefineConstants>$(DefineConstants);ENABLE_LOGGING</DefineConstants>
```

---

### 5. `LibA/LibA.csproj` (lines 43–45) — Self-invoking `<MSBuild>` task re-enters the same project

```xml
<Target Name="PublishOnBuild" AfterTargets="Build">
  <MSBuild Projects="$(MSBuildProjectFullPath)" Targets="Publish" Properties="_IsPublishing=true" />
</Target>
```

**Problem:** This forks a **second evaluation** of the same project with an extra global property (`_IsPublishing=true`), creating a distinct project instance. Both instances write to the same `OutputPath`/`IntermediateOutputPath`, causing:
- Race conditions with file writes between the two instances
- Double-build overhead (full rebuild, not just publish)
- Potential `IOException` "file in use" errors on CI

**Fix:** Use `DependsOnTargets` to run Publish within the same project instance, or invoke `dotnet publish` as a separate build step in CI instead of embedding it in the build.

---

### 6. `fsharp/BrokenOrder/BrokenOrder.fsproj` (lines 7–9) — Incorrect F# file compilation order

```xml
<Compile Include="Services.fs" />   <!-- uses Domain types -->
<Compile Include="Domain.fs" />     <!-- defines Domain types -->
<Compile Include="Program.fs" />    <!-- uses Services -->
```

**Problem:** F# compilation order is determined by the order of `<Compile>` items. `Services.fs` opens `BrokenOrder.Domain`, but `Domain.fs` (which defines the `Domain` module) is listed **after** it. This will produce a compilation error: `FS0039: The namespace or module 'BrokenOrder.Domain' is not defined`.

**Fix:** Reorder to match dependencies (as done correctly in `OrderService.fsproj`):
```xml
<Compile Include="Domain.fs" />
<Compile Include="Services.fs" />
<Compile Include="Program.fs" />
```

---

## 🟡 Warnings (anti-patterns that should be fixed)

### 7. `LibA/LibA.csproj` (lines 27–29) — Raw assembly `<Reference>` with hardcoded HintPath

```xml
<Reference Include="Newtonsoft.Json">
  <HintPath>..\packages\Newtonsoft.Json.13.0.3\lib\net6.0\Newtonsoft.Json.dll</HintPath>
</Reference>
```

**Problem:** This is a legacy `packages.config`-style reference in an SDK-style project. The path `..\packages\...` is the old NuGet packages folder layout, which doesn't exist with `PackageReference`. This reference will fail to resolve at build time (no such directory).

**Fix:** Replace with a proper PackageReference:
```xml
<PackageReference Include="Newtonsoft.Json" Version="13.0.3" />
```

---

### 8. `LibA/LibA.csproj` (line 7) and `LibB/LibB.csproj` (line 7) — Hardcoded Windows-only `OutputPath`

```xml
<OutputPath>C:\builds\output\LibA</OutputPath>
<OutputPath>C:\builds\output\LibB</OutputPath>
```

**Problem:** These are absolute Windows paths (`C:\...`). They will fail on Linux/macOS CI agents and break for any developer whose machine doesn't have this path. They also bypass the standard `bin/$(Configuration)/$(TargetFramework)/` convention, which breaks IDE tooling expectations.

**Fix:** Remove these lines and rely on SDK defaults, or use relative paths:
```xml
<OutputPath>bin\$(Configuration)\$(TargetFramework)\</OutputPath>
```

---

### 9. `Directory.Build.props` (lines 16–18) — Analyzer package missing `PrivateAssets="all"`

```xml
<PackageReference Include="StyleCop.Analyzers" Version="1.2.0-beta.556" />
```

**Problem:** Without `PrivateAssets="all"`, this analyzer package becomes a transitive dependency. Any project that references LibA or LibB will also pull in StyleCop.Analyzers as a runtime dependency, bloating deployment and potentially causing assembly-loading conflicts. Analyzers should never flow downstream.

**Fix:**
```xml
<PackageReference Include="StyleCop.Analyzers" Version="1.2.0-beta.556">
  <PrivateAssets>all</PrivateAssets>
  <IncludeAssets>runtime; build; native; contentfiles; analyzers</IncludeAssets>
</PackageReference>
```

---

### 10. `LibA/LibA.csproj` (lines 21–24) — Redundant `Include` + `Update` in same ItemGroup

```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <Compile Include="Class1.cs" />
  <Compile Update="Class1.cs" AutoGen="true" />
</ItemGroup>
```

**Problem:** The SDK already auto-includes all `*.cs` files. The explicit `Include` creates a **duplicate** `Compile` entry for `Class1.cs`, which may trigger `CS2002` ("Source file specified multiple times") warnings. The `Update` in the same ItemGroup then applies metadata to only one of the two entries.

**Fix:** Remove the `Include` entirely; use only `Update`:
```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <Compile Update="Class1.cs" AutoGen="true" />
</ItemGroup>
```

---

### 11. No Central Package Management (CPM)

**Problem:** Package versions are scattered across individual project files (`Directory.Build.props` has `StyleCop.Analyzers 1.2.0-beta.556`, LibA has the raw Newtonsoft.Json reference). As the solution grows, version drift becomes inevitable.

**Fix:** Create a `Directory.Packages.props` at the repo root with `<ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>true</ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>` and centralize all `Version` attributes there.

---

## 🔵 Suggestions (style/maintainability improvements)

### 12. `StyleIssues.sln` — F# projects not included in solution

The solution only includes LibA and LibB. The two F# projects (`fsharp/BrokenOrder` and `fsharp/OrderService`) are not in the `.sln`. This means `dotnet build StyleIssues.sln` won't build them, potentially hiding build errors (like the BrokenOrder compilation order bug above).

**Suggestion:** Add the F# projects to the solution or create a separate solution for the F# sub-tree.

---

### 13. `LibA/LibA.csproj` (line 33) — Exec command has hardcoded version string

```xml
<Exec Command="echo Building version 1.0.0" />
```

This will be stale the moment the version changes. If version logging is needed, use `$(Version)` or `$(PackageVersion)`:
```xml
<Exec Command="echo Building version $(Version)" />
```

---

### 14. `fsharp/Directory.Build.props` and `fsharp/Directory.Build.targets` — Empty files that block inheritance

These files are intentionally empty to prevent the root `Directory.Build.props/targets` (C#-specific) from leaking into the F# projects. This works but is fragile — if someone adds a repo-wide setting to the root files expecting it to apply everywhere, the F# projects silently won't receive it.

**Suggestion:** Instead of empty files, use `<Import>` with selective filtering:
```xml
<!-- fsharp/Directory.Build.props -->
<Project>
  <Import Project="$([MSBuild]::GetPathOfFileAbove('Directory.Build.props', '$(MSBuildThisFileDirectory)../'))" />
  <!-- Override C#-specific settings here -->
  <PropertyGroup>
    <StyleCopEnabled>false</StyleCopEnabled>
  </PropertyGroup>
</Project>
```

---

- **SDK-style projects throughout** — All projects use the modern SDK-style format. No legacy `<Import Project="$(MSBuildToolsPath)...">`patterns.
- **`fsharp/OrderService/OrderService.fsproj`** — Correct F# file ordering (`Domain.fs` → `Services.fs` → `Program.fs`), showing the team knows the pattern.
- **F# isolation via nested `Directory.Build.*` files** — The intent to isolate F# projects from C#-specific build settings is sound architecture, even if the implementation could be improved.
- **Single TFM** — All projects target `net8.0`, avoiding unnecessary multi-targeting complexity.

| Severity | Count | Key Themes |

| 🔴 Error | 6 | TFM condition in `.props`, property override in `.targets`, unquoted condition, constants overwrite, self-invoking MSBuild task, F# file order |
